facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face
left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision
pain on palpation
no fever or chills
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face
Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
nests of highly atypical cells
Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
Telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast carcinoma with metastasis, and the current symptoms and histopathological examination suggest cutaneous metastasis.
The presence of telangiectasia, nests of highly atypical cells, and positive CD31 staining suggest angiosarcoma.
The patient's history of breast carcinoma and the presence of telangiectasia and metastatic cells suggest telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma.
The presence of telangiectasia, nests of highly atypical cells, and positive CD31 staining suggest primary cutaneous angiosarcoma.

rationales.F02: History of breast carcinoma increases likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F04: Previous metastasis to lymph nodes increases likelihood of further metastasis.
rationales.F07: Telangiectatic appearance is common in both cutaneous metastasis and angiosarcoma.
rationales.F09: Presence of highly atypical cells is indicative of malignancy.
rationales.F10: CD31 positivity is consistent with vascular origin of the tumor cells.
rationales.F11: GATA3 positivity is highly specific for breast carcinoma origin.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of left breast carcinoma and metastasis, combined with the presence of telangiectasia and nests of highly atypical cells in the dermis, supports this diagnosis.
